body:
WHAT
One user message drives one turn: the engine streams the model's thinking and text to the frontend as it arrives, collects tool calls, runs them (read-only calls in parallel, mutating calls in order), appends the results as a user message, and calls the model again until it ends without tool calls. The turn emits exactly one turn_started and one turn_finished event (with stopReason and usage) and records every message to the transcript.

WHY
This is the core agent loop; without it the model cannot act on the workspace, and without a single well-formed turn end the frontend cannot know when to re-enable input.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.runTurn() (busy flag, turn_started, `for (let iteration = 0; ; iteration++)` loop, pushMessage, turn_finished in finally), Session.streamAssistantTurn() (provider.stream → text_delta / thinking_delta / tool_use_* / message_end handling, stats.recordResponse), Session.executeToolCalls() (schema parse, permissions.check, tool.execute, tool_call_started/finished events, parallel vs sequential batches), Session.buildSystemPrompt(), Session.toolSchemas(), Session.pushMessage(). Provider contract: engine/providers/src/fake.ts FakeProvider for tests.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. With a FakeProvider scripted [{thinking:'hmm', text:'Reading', toolCalls:[Read x]}, {text:'Done.'}], runTurn emits thinking_delta 'hmm', text_delta chunks concatenating to 'Reading' then 'Done.', one tool_call_started and one tool_call_finished for Read, and exactly one turn_started and one turn_finished (stopReason 'end_turn').
2. The second provider request's messages are [user text, assistant {thinking, text, tool_use}, user {tool_result with matching toolUseId}] — the tool result is appended before the model is called again.
3. Calling runTurn while a turn is running rejects with 'session is already processing a turn'; after the turn isBusy() is false.
4. A batch of two Read calls plus one Write runs the reads concurrently and the Write sequentially, and results are returned in the original call order with matching toolUseIds.
5. An unknown tool name or invalid input produces an isError tool_result with a descriptive message and the loop continues to the next model call rather than throwing; a provider error (FakeTurn.error) ends the turn with stopReason 'error' and an error event, still emitting turn_finished.
